title: Not in the Name of Pride
description: Not in the Name of Pride in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 155, “Presence of Jesus”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Not in the name of pride Or self-ish-ness we're met; From world-ly paths we turn a-side, And world-ly thoughts for-get.

lines: Not in the name of pride
From worldly paths we turn aside,
Thou in the midst of us shalt be,
Now, Lord, let every bounding heart
And bid our inmost souls rejoice

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
